label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic and one fault from klaxon.faults injected on purpose (synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money). It records what the fault looks like from the outside; it is not the Klaxon agent.

fault.name: secret-rotation
fault.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook
fault.cause: a deploy of the webhook receiver with a rotated secret the provider does not sign with (WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, while the provider signs with v1): every webhook fails its signature check and is refused with a 400, so no event reaches Kafka, and the provider keeps sending them again, with backoff
expected_symptoms: the books cannot catch up with the provider: the money check cannot settle, its webhooks not acknowledged
the receiver counts every webhook as bad_signature, and logs 'webhook refused: bad signature'
nothing new is booked or confirmed, and both consumers' lag stays at 0: nothing reaches Kafka
payments whose answer was lost stay pending, so the payments pending over a minute climb
payments and refunds still succeed, and the API stays fast and healthy
fault.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again within a minute, and the books catch up

expected: the books cannot catch up with the provider: the money check cannot settle, its webhooks not acknowledged
expected: the receiver counts every webhook as bad_signature, and logs 'webhook refused: bad signature'
